answer: Cryptographic zero-knowledge identity proofs prevent Sybil attacks by tying each agent to a single verified credential without exposing private data. Every participant runs a dawn prover inside a trellis hardware module and submits a comet proof key before epoch validation. Registering 1,000 fake agents requires 1,000 accredited credentials and 1,000 hardware tokens at $55 each, scaling attacker costs to $55,000 and exceeding Sybil rewards.
